\section{One}

{\bf The main Theorem A}\quad Every compact space is bounded.

{\bf Theorem 1.1}\quad Every finite space is compact.

{\bf Proof.}\quad Cover the space by finitely many sets. $\Box$

{\bf Theorem 1.2}\quad Every closed part of a compact space is compact.

{\bf Proof.}\quad Take a cover of the part. $\Box$

{\bf alternative Proof :}\quad Use nets instead of covers. $\Box$

Some text between them.

{\bf An alternative proof of Theorem 1.1}: \quad Count the points of the space. $\Box$
